items.title: Global Payments (GPN) Stock Fair Value Edges Higher After Analysts Reset Q2 Views
items.summary: The average fair value price target for Global Payments has shifted to US$104.39 from US$101.71, reflecting the latest round of analyst model updates. This change aligns with recent Street research that incorporates Q2 results, new segment disclosures, and refreshed 2026 to 2027 frameworks, along with a range of individual price targets that extend into the US$110 to US$125 area. As you read on, you will see how these revisions fit into the evolving narrative around Global Payments and what...

items.title: How Has Visa's Growth Story Changed?
items.summary: Visa's management tells its growth story differently than it did two years ago. That matters for your money. The shares cost 31 times a year of earnings, against 22.4 times for the S&P 500. A price that high assumes the growth keeps coming. One label that used to feature in Visa's results has faded. Which part of the business did Visa's management use to highlight in its quarterly results.

items.title: Can Global Payments Gain From Growing Consumer Trust in AI Commerce?
items.summary: GPN is positioned to support agent-led commerce as consumers show greater comfort letting AI make everyday purchases.

items.title: Can Visa Stock Keep Climbing After The World Cup?
items.summary: Visa (V) stock has run well ahead of the market, returning 13.5% over the past three months against 4.2% for the S&P 500. It now trades about 4% below its 52-week high. The next leg depends less on card swipes than on the services Visa sells on top of its network, which now bring in almost a third of its revenue.

items.title: Can Genius Emerge as a Key Growth Driver for Global Payments?
items.summary: GPN is ramping up Genius, integrating payments, POS and software to expand its reach among SMBs and drive recurring revenues.

items.title: Can Worldpay Help Global Payments Build a Stronger Growth Story?
items.summary: GPN's Worldpay integration is reshaping its growth strategy, with stronger margins and broader payment capabilities offering new avenues for expansion.

items.title: How Is Global Payments' Stock Performance Compared to Other Industrial Stocks?
items.summary: While Global Payments has outperformed relative to its peers over the past year, Wall Street analysts maintain a cautiously optimistic outlook on its prospects.

items.title: Here Are Friday’s Top Wall Street Analyst Research Calls: Atmos Energy, Celanese, Check Point Software, Chewy, Dell Technologies, Fortinet, Global Payments, HP, Shopify, and More
